maria (eng-runtime): heads-up — saw a regression in production traces for long-context jobs (>4k tokens). latency p99 climbs and HBM bandwidth is pegged. suspecting a KV-chain scan + kernel-choice oscillation.

jonah (perf): can you paste the nsys summary? curious if it's pure DRAM/PCIe or kernel scheduling churn.

maria (eng-runtime): pasted below — this is from the 2nd worker on a 4xA100 dedicated node, one of the heavy tails: ```nsys summary
Total GPU Time: 38.75ms
dram__throughput.avg.pct_of_peak_sustained_elapsed: 94.1%
l1tex__t_sectors_pipe_lsu_mem_atomic_op_tex_mem_global_avg.pct_of_peak_sustained_elapsed: 12.3%
sm__cycles_elapsed.avg.pct_of_peak_sustained_elapsed: 28.7%
Kernel timeline: heavy alternating small-kernel spikes (~0.8ms) and long KV-page-copy kernels (~7-10ms)```

maria (eng-runtime): trace also shows repeated KV cache misses cascading: a hot token stream forces a chain of page reads, but our kernel selector keeps switching between small attention kernels and large memcpy-ish kernels. results in short kernels starving SM, long kernels saturating HBM, then back.

lena (eng-infra): that oscillation smell: bandwidth up, compute low. could be DMA engine getting saturated and blocking small compute kernels. do we see DMA stall counters?

maria (eng-runtime): yes — counter snapshot: ```nvprof counters
memcpy.h2d_throughput: 9.8 GB/s
memcpy.d2d_throughput: 41.2 GB/s
nvlink: 0.5 GB/s
dma.stalls: 73% (sampled)```

jonah (perf): interesting — so the KV page kernel is effectively serializing accesses. Two thoughts: 1) change kernel selection policy to prefer fused KV-copy+compute kernels for long sequences (eliminate standalone memcpy kernel), 2) adapt microbatching so KV hot-path stays resident (reduce interleaving across requests).

kai (serving): option 1 needs more kernel engineering. option 2 might be faster to test: tweak batcher to keep same request's microbatches contiguous until KV cache warm. we already track per-request KV hit-rate; we can add a short affinity window.

maria (eng-runtime): tried an A/B local run with affinity window = 300ms, hit-rate for long runs improved from 62% -> 89% and p99 dropped ~28%. cpu-side latencies increased slightly due to holding batches, but net token cost down.

jonah (perf): can you share the perfetto snippet? want to inspect the kernel switching timeline to verify it's not scheduling artifact.

maria (eng-runtime): perfetto link (internal): https://perfetto.local/trace/59f3 — tl;dr: pattern is [copy-kernel ~8ms] -> [tiny-attn ~0.6ms x 6] -> [copy-kernel], repeating. zoom shows copy-kernel saturates dram throughput per GPU to ~92% of peak.

lena (eng-infra): could NUMA / placement be amplifying this? are the KV pages pinned to same GPU? if pages migrate between GPUs, cross-GPU traffic might add to stalls.

maria (eng-runtime): we checked pinning: pages are on local HBMs but page grouping sometimes scatters due to our allocator's stripe policy under high alloc/free churn. changed freelist to favor contiguous allocations for KV pages and saw small improvement.

jonah (perf): two parallel experiments to run: 1) kernel fusion path prototype that merges small-attn + page-copy when sequence > threshold, 2) batcher affinity window rollout with telemetry. prioritize 2 for short turnaround.

kai (serving): i'll flip a canary with affinity window = 300ms on a Dedicated shard and add a metric: kv_chain_miss_ratio_by_seq_len. also add a flag to enable kernel-fusion opt-in.

maria (eng-runtime): logged the canary results in staging: p95 down 18%, p99 down 35% for >4k seqs; CPU sleep/time-to-first-token up ~5ms. recording as follow-up work to prototype fused kernels.

perf-bot: experiment recorded — id=exp/2026-11-02/kv-affinity-300ms, baseline_vs_candidate: p99 0.65x, notes: improved kv hit-rate for long sequences.

jonah (perf): nice. next steps: schedule kernel-fusion spike with eng-ml; also add automated nsys sampling for sequences >3k to catch regressions early. i'll add a perf alert rule for dram__throughput.avg.pct_of_peak_sustained_elapsed > 88% for >60s.

maria (eng-runtime): agree. i'll open a PR with batcher change + telemetry and add the canary config. leaving some TODOs in the PR for kernel fusion spike. thanks y'all :thumbsup:
